lineage: Successor of the v0.1.0 label set released with danielrosehill/Voice-Note-Intent-Classifier (9 flat labels). v0.2.0 splits labels into `route` and `tag` kinds and adds meeting_notes and dev_spec. Changing a label's kind is a major change under the versioning rules in docs/spec.md, so this would be 1.0.0 if v0.1.0 had been frozen; it was a draft, so it is a minor bump.

semantics.multi_label: Every label is an independent yes/no. A transcript can carry several routes and several tags at once.
semantics.nullable: Both lists may be empty. Empty `routes` with abstain=false means the note is confidently not actionable and is filed to the default inbox. abstain=true means the model is unsure and the router falls back to the rung-0 LLM router.
semantics.route: A route label has a downstream subagent with its own role prompt and MCP tool. The router dispatches the transcript once per route label that clears its threshold.
semantics.tag: A tag label is metadata only. It never triggers a dispatch. It exists so one classifier can do routing and loose tagging in a single pass. A tag can be promoted to a route later (minor version bump) once a subagent exists for it.

labels.name: Shopping list
labels.definition: Items to buy. One or more products, quantities optional, no further action requested.

labels.name: To-do
labels.definition: One or more tasks the speaker (or someone they name) needs to do, with no fixed time slot. A due date may be mentioned.

labels.name: Calendar event
labels.definition: Something happening at a specific date/time that should occupy a slot: an appointment, meeting, booking, deadline-as-event.

labels.name: Email draft
labels.definition: Dictated text intended to be sent as an email, usually with a recipient and an addressing/sign-off structure, or an explicit instruction to write one.

labels.name: Content draft
labels.definition: Material for publication — blog post, blog outline, article, social post, video script — as opposed to private notes.

labels.name: Meeting notes
labels.definition: Minutes or a debrief of a meeting or call that happened, or an agenda/prep for one that has not happened yet.

labels.name: AI prompt
labels.definition: Instructions addressed to an AI system to be run now — a prompt, system prompt, or task for a model or agent.

labels.name: Development spec / project outline
labels.definition: A description of something to be built — software, a model, a system — with its purpose, scope and requirements, meant to be filed as a project document rather than executed immediately.

labels.name: Note to self
labels.definition: Information to remember or file — a fact, a location, an observation. Nothing needs doing.

labels.name: Idea
labels.definition: A single discrete concept captured for later — a product, project, feature, or business idea — stated briefly.

labels.name: Brainstorm
labels.definition: Extended exploratory thinking out loud: weighing options, open questions, several half-formed ideas around one problem.

confusable_pairs.rule: Does it need a slot? 'Call the plumber' is todo; 'plumber coming Tuesday at ten' is calendar_event. A task with a due date stays todo.
Is there an action? 'The router password is on the sticker' is a note; 'change the router password' is a todo.
One discrete concept stated briefly is idea; open-ended reasoning across options is brainstorm. Length is a signal, not the rule.
Is it for an audience? Thinking for yourself is brainstorm; dictating something to publish is content_draft, however rough.
An email has a recipient and is sent; a content draft is published or filed.
Who does the work? Instructions addressed to an AI are ai_prompt; a task the speaker will do is todo. 'Write me a to-do list app' is ai_prompt.
'Write an email to the landlord about the boiler' is labelled email_draft only: the email route has to act, and its subagent composes from instructions as well as dictation.
Execute now vs file for later. A spec addressed to an agent with 'go and build this' is ai_prompt; a description of a project to be written up and filed is dev_spec. Both may apply.
A spec converges on what is to be built; a brainstorm stays open. A long spec that weighs options can carry dev_spec plus the brainstorm tag.
An idea is one line of concept; a spec has scope, requirements or an architecture. The idea tag may accompany dev_spec.
Prep for a future meeting is meeting_notes; booking the slot is calendar_event. A note that does both carries both.

candidates.definition: A short message for WhatsApp/SMS/Slack rather than email.
candidates.reason: Different routing target and register from email_draft.

candidates.definition: A nudge tied to a time or place, not a task list item or a calendar slot.
candidates.reason: Overlaps todo and calendar_event; may resolve as a field on those instead of a label.
Appeared in every earlier taxonomy; would be a tag first.

candidates.definition: A question to look up or investigate.
candidates.reason: Borderline; may fold into ai_prompt since the route is an AI query.

candidates.definition: A purchase, receipt or expense to record.
Contact details to save — a name with a phone, email or address.
candidates.reason: Routes to a contacts integration; distinct action.
